title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need
lede: Bengaluru's Humyn Labs records people doing everyday tasks on its own two-camera rig and sells the labelled footage to US labs and robotics companies training physical AI.

points: The $47 million Series A splits into $26 million of Accel-led equity and $21 million of venture debt.
Its software tracks hand movement and object interactions, turning raw recordings into training data.
Collection runs in over 20 countries across Latin America and Asia, centred on Brazil, India and South Korea, via the founders' KGeN network.
It has 12 paying customers, including frontier labs and world-model developers, and earned $10 million from April to October, about 90% from the US.
The debt bridges paying collectors daily or weekly while waiting 30 to 60 days for lab customers to pay.

sections.text: Real-world human video is a bottleneck for robot learning, and filming inside homes raises consent and privacy questions that teams buying such datasets will have to weigh.
